title: Explicit Multi-Workspace Publication Proposals
summary: A shared publication selects an immutable local candidate without changing its source route/workspace provenance. Submission, review, resolution and retrieval remain separate operations.
scope: P3E11 uses existing locally prepared managed artifacts and HTTP. No remote source upload, WebSocket, Desktop/tray, dashboard design, MCP, consumer migration or Git merge.
identity: Source routes remain bound to a single workspace/profile. A publication is a separate project-scoped name with a monotonic shared head. Candidates from different registered local source routes may compete for that head. Retrieval reports the selected source identity; it never relabels a different worktree as the caller's current source.

api.head: GET at prefix returns compact head metadata, never artifact paths/keys or source freshness claims.
api.submit: POST proposals with preparation_id, base_revision and the reviewed history_epoch; omission means epoch0, not automatic current admission. Legacy HTTP Idempotency-Key remains principal-wide within the NULL-scope domain. Schema025 native scoped submissions use principal/project/history_workspace_id/key in a disjoint domain; see shin-workspace-ownership-v1. The candidate belongs to the project and caller or administrator. Store validates and captures immutable candidate/base provenance; a positive new base must still be retained. Client-supplied origin is rejected; submission never activates or runs a job. Retained exact replay precedes filesystem/capacity admission; discarded old requests are rejected by the epoch fence in shin-publication-history-v1.
api.list: GET proposals accepts bounded after/limit pagination; GET proposals/{id} returns captured base, observed current head, candidate metadata and immutable resolution if any. Conflict is derived from an unresolved proposal's base versus the head, never a read-side write.
api.review: GET proposals/{id}/review verifies available artifact bytes with Core using immutable saved provenance, not the current source catalog. Historical comparison works after source route reconfiguration or source disappearance. Candidate and Core publication read locks for each admitted artifact remain held through the complete bounded comparison and final ledger reread. Compare only sides marked artifact-verified. One concurrent review, at most three bounded artifacts, 32 detailed changes per comparison and 32768 detail bytes globally; omissions are explicit. Missing retired artifacts remain unavailable. No source-currentness, semantic-equivalence or publication-permit claim.
api.resolve: POST proposals/{id}/resolution with exact decision (accept/reject/request-reprepare) and expected_revision. Administrator only. A retained proposal's same terminal decision and consumed revision replay its receipt; a different retry conflicts, and explicitly retired proposal IDs remain not-found. request-reprepare records advice and closes this proposal but does not execute preparation.
api.retrieval: POST search/brief/pack at the publication prefix reuses native retrieval and its bounds for the selected immutable artifact, with explicit publication_id, source route/workspace and admitted revision. It does not depend on that source route's separate active selection.

transportProjection: Shared publication and existing route retrieval omit only CLI-local top-level root/out_root coordinates. All canonical evidence records, verification paths and receipt hashes are preserved. Source identity is explicit in the Server wrapper. A changed source route still blocks retrieval and new acceptance; historical artifact review never grants an exception.
lifecycleBoundary: P3E11 originally had no shared-head withdrawal. Its successor shin-publication-withdrawal-v1 defines explicit withdrawal, persisted withdrawn revisions and typed proposal bases in schema 013. Publication-history pruning remains separate; full proposal history returns capacity diagnostics, never TTL eviction. Withdrawal does not require spare proposal capacity. SQL-seeded quota fixtures do not claim all seeded artifacts were built or served.

transactions.submit: Serialize bounded publication admission, lock candidate/base preparations in ID order, reject retention intent, then insert proposal and audit together. A stale but known shared base is retained as a conflicted proposal rather than overwritten or discarded.
transactions.accept: Rerun existing candidate structural/source/quality checks, holding artifact lifetime/publication locks through a short database transaction. Lock order: activation writers, publication writers, candidate preparation, audit writers. Check source base, candidate binding and expected shared revision again; insert immutable resolution and update shared head with audit atomically. Audit rows carry a typed publication_proposal_id foreign key, including submit/reject/request-reprepare, rather than relying on ambiguous action text.
transactions.conflict: Two accept requests consuming the same shared revision cannot both commit. The losing unresolved proposal remains visible. A later deliberate acceptance requires reviewing and supplying the new head revision; quality is rerun, not inferred from an earlier report.
transactions.retention: Unresolved proposals pin their candidate and captured base artifacts; the current shared head pins its selected artifact. Rejection/request-reprepare releases proposal pins only. Accepted old history remains metadata and does not indefinitely pin retired artifacts. Existing descriptor locks still protect admitted readers.
transactions.recovery: A lost reply is handled by stable identity/replay. Restart does not lose proposals, conflicts or decisions. PostgreSQL unavailability cannot erase local Observer state. Source-bearing synchronization remains a later explicit protocol.
